How to choose a slow cooker for everyday meals

Think about the meal you want ready when you get home, how many people it needs to feed and where the cooker will sit. A larger pot is useful only if it suits your normal recipes and you have room to lift, wash and store it.

Capacity in quarts: compare the pot, not just the headline

Check the usable fill range in the exact manual rather than treating the advertised capacity as a serving guarantee. A deep round pot and a wide oval pot can accommodate different ingredients. For batch cooking, consider how you will portion and store the finished meal as well as how much fits inside the cooker.

Manual dial or programmable timer?

A simple dial may suit a routine where someone is home to switch the cooker off. A programmable model is worth comparing when you need a defined cooking time, but check what happens afterwards: automatic keep-warm, a manual warm setting and delayed start are different functions. Do not assume that every digital display includes all three.

For example, Crock-Pot describes its manual 8-quart model as offering High, Low and Warm settings. That is a control example for that model, not proof that every listing above has a timer or automatic keep-warm. Source: Crock-Pot manual 8-quart model specifications.

Searing, cleaning and the weight of a full pot

If you want to brown ingredients in the same vessel, confirm that the exact insert is approved for your hob or stove. A removable bowl alone does not establish this. Check which parts are dishwasher-safe, how the handles are held and whether the pot fits in your sink. Follow the model instructions for cooking and cleaning.

Compare running costs for your actual recipe

Compare power use and cooking time for the same meal; a low wattage label alone does not establish the total cost. A slow cooker and a pressure multi-cooker also offer different cooking methods. Choose the functions you will use rather than paying for a longer mode list.

What makes a cheaper offer worth buying?

Check the model number, pot and lid condition, included accessories, local voltage, warranty and returns. With used or refurbished stock, a replacement pot or lid can change the apparent saving. Reviews are most useful when they discuss the exact model, normal meal size, controls and cleaning; seller feedback concerns the transaction.

eBay vs Amazon: where should you compare?

For Slow Cookers, it is worth checking both retailers rather than assuming one is always cheaper. eBay can be useful for new, refurbished and open-box stock and exposes seller feedback clearly. Amazon can be useful for comparing new-stock availability, delivery options and retailer returns where offered. Always compare the exact model number, condition, warranty, delivery cost and returns policy before deciding.

Buying questions answered

What size slow cooker should I buy?

Compare your usual recipe and the manufacturer’s recommended fill range. Headline capacity alone does not guarantee a number of servings.

Does a slow cooker switch to warm automatically?

Only some models do. Check the exact controls and what happens at the end of the cooking time before relying on this feature.

Can I brown ingredients in the slow cooker pot?

Only when the manufacturer approves the exact insert for that hob or stove. Removable does not automatically mean hob-safe.

Is a slow cooker the same as a pressure cooker?

No. A multi-cooker may offer both methods, but check the supported modes and recipe instructions for the appliance.
